Tasks: 101 SWE-CoWork tasks with identical task definitions, repository states and executable contracts. Configurations: 11 models in CoWork (GPT-6 Astra on Codex, the other 10 on Claude Code), all at max effort; same colleague model (GPT-5.6 Terra, high effort) for all agents; 8-hour execution budget; same onboarding note per task. Baseline/control: Oracle-Spec (complete requirements upfront, no colleagues) for Seed Evolving and GPT-6 Astra, holding tasks, repository, tests, scaffold and budget constant. Acceptance tests: private F2P/P2P tests. Repetitions: not stated (one recorded run per task per model apparently). Human intervention: none

Claude-Opus-5.5 highest F2P (63.84%) and GPT-6 Astra highest Pass rate (7.92%); the other nine models at most 39.09% F2P and 0.99% Pass rate; P2P 81.85-95.20% with a different ranking. Requirement acquisition is strongly associated with F2P (Spearman rho = 0.94, 11 models), tool calls are not (rho = 0.08); earlier first edit (rho = -0.62) and more colleague messages (rho = 0.71) associate with higher F2P (8 models). Oracle-Spec raises F2P by +16.67 pp (Seed Evolving) and +15.93 pp (GPT-6 Astra); P2P -4.98 / +2.66 pp; Pass rate unchanged (+0.00). Claude-Opus-5.5: 31% of requirements reported done fail their tests; 153 of 450 deferred threads not followed up. No significance tests of differences; associations described as non-causal

Distinguished models clearly on F2P (13.04-63.84%) and on requirement acquisition; Pass rate near floor (0-7.92%) and barely discriminates. Repeatability not assessed (no repetitions reported). Limitations of the method stated by the authors: simulated colleagues may differ from human users (mitigated by fixed knowledge boundaries and disclosure rules); cross-model associations do not establish causation; input-token totals include repeated context; usage telemetry missing for DeepSeek V4 Pro and Seed 2.1 Pro

No limitations or threats-to-validity section. Caveats: associations are exploratory and non-causal; the Oracle-Spec F2P gain mixes direct access to requirements with search effort saved. Gaps: sustained requirement tracking (owner, open questions, implementation status, verification evidence, handoff claims) is a key open challenge; whether explicit tracking improves end-to-end delivery is open; extend to teams of autonomous agents
